items.title: 1 of Wall Street’s Favorite Stocks to Own for Decades and 2 We Ignore
items.summary: The stocks in this article have caught Wall Street’s attention in a big way, with price targets implying returns above 20%. But investors should take these forecasts with a grain of salt because analysts typically say nice things about companies so their firms can win business in other product lines like M&A advisory.

items.title: Signet Jewelers Surges 14% as Raised Profit Outlook Overrides Flat Sales Guidance, Tapestry Holds Steady
items.summary: Signet Jewelers just posted its sixth straight earnings beat and sent its stock soaring, but the company held its full-year sales guidance flat, leaving investors to decide whether the profit story alone justifies chasing a stock already up big on the year.

items.title: 3 S&P 500 Stocks That Fall Short
items.summary: The S&P 500 (^GSPC) is often seen as a benchmark for strong businesses, but that doesn’t mean every stock is worth owning. Some companies face significant challenges, whether it’s stagnating growth, heavy debt, or disruptive new competitors.

items.title: The Top 5 Analyst Questions From Tapestry’s Q2 Earnings Call
items.summary: Tapestry’s second quarter was marked by steady top-line growth and improved profitability, but the market responded negatively as investors weighed future risks and moderating growth expectations. Management attributed the revenue gains to strong customer acquisition, particularly among Gen Z consumers, and continued traction in the core leather goods segment. items.title: Gap taps Coach architect Reed Krakoff for $29.95-$498 handbag line
items.summary: Tapestry (NYSE: TPR), whose Coach brand Krakoff himself helped build, is the most direct equity expression of that competitive pressure. Coach accounts for the majority of Tapestry’s revenue, and any meaningful share Gap captures in the accessible-luxury bag segment would come at the expense of Tapestry’s core customer.
